clue.text: Official recommends eliminating rook sanctuaries

parts.note: REF is short for referee, a match official

indicators.note: taking out the chess piece's letter from the verb for recommending

parts.note: to recommend a course is to urge it
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat advises closing down bird refuges for rooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminating rook' takes R out of URGES, leaving UGES to follow REF.
explanation.definitionFit: Places of shelter and safety are havens, the same idea as sanctuaries.

clue.text: Agent given musical piece responded

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent for a firm
a Lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: Someone's representative answers after being handed a song.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer back is to have responded; both are past-tense verbs of reply.

clue.text: Discharge associated with high-level report?

parts.note: an electrical discharge in the sky, branching into zigzags, that comes with thunder: the 'high-level report' is a thunderclap rather than a document from senior staff

explanation.walkthrough: 'report' reads as a written document from the top brass, but it is the bang of thunder overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Branching bolts of electricity during a storm are a discharge whose bang is heard high up as thunder.

clue.text: Illuminated folder one GI brandished

indicators.note: something brandished is waved about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier waves around a decorated document folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brandished' rearranges FOLDER, I and GI.
explanation.definitionFit: An illuminated manuscript is decorated and glorified with gold and colour; both mean adorned or exalted.

clue.text: Quick note

definitions.meaning: a note raised a semitone in music

explanation.definitionFit: A quick mind is keen, and in music a raised semitone note carries the same name.

clue.text: Sound measure for dealing with bed lice

indicators.note: dealing suggests sharing out cards, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A noise level reading is taken while treating a bed infested with lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing with' rearranges BEDLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of loudness is the standard way sound intensity is measured.

clue.text: Adopting a view that's making approaches

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: drives, as in drives someone mad, means makes
a way of seeing things is a view or opinion

explanation.surface: Someone taking on an outlook is busy making overtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopting' puts WAY inside DRIVES; 'a' and 'that's' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: Private roads leading up to houses are the approaches to them.

clue.text: Furry creature at first shy, then jumping up

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

indicators.note: jumping suggests the two letters leaping about into another order

explanation.surface: A timid animal suddenly leaps to its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges UP to PU; 'at first' and 'then' just set the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American aquatic rodent with thick fur is an example of a furry animal.

clue.text: Furry creature at first Greens in the EU?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Furry creature at first Greens in the EU?', which repeats the start of 6-down; the printed clue for BRUSSELS SPROUTS is garbled in the OCR and no scan or search gives its true wording.
annotationWithheld.clue: Furry creature at first Greens in the EU?

clue.text: Public worship perverted by guilty Rector

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Church services are corrupted by a rector with a bad conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' rearranges GUILTY to LITURGY's first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed form of communal Christian service is the order of public worship.

clue.text: US plot certainly involved adulation of political leader

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American conspiracy is surely tied up with hero-worship of a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges all fifteen letters of US PLOT CERTAINLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive glorification of a ruler, as under dictators, is this kind of devotion.

clue.text: Tribe hostile to Roman influence rocks Northern Ireland

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink on the rocks

explanation.surface: A tribe opposed to Rome shakes up Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were a British tribe led by Boudicca in revolt against Roman rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca's people in eastern Britain rose against the Roman occupiers.

clue.text: Early indication showing river's source, perhaps, in Puerto Rico

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the abbreviation for Puerto Rico

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible rearrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A sign of things to come reveals where a Puerto Rican river begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges R and SOURCE to ECURSOR, which goes 'in' PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner or harbinger is an early sign of something to come.

clue.text: Priest's daughter one left in place of bishop in US state

indicators.note: in place of means one thing replaces another, here letters swap for the chess bishop

parts.note: Alabama is a state in the US South
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is one in Roman numerals and L stands for left

explanation.surface: A clergyman's daughter replaces a bishop in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' swaps the B of ALABAMA for IL, giving ALAILAMA after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet's spiritual leader is a high Buddhist cleric, a lama, so a priest.

clue.text: Anyone can set out to cause irritation

indicators.note: set out means arranged anew, so these letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Anybody is able to start being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges ANYONECAN; 'to cause' is a linking phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation or bother is a feeling of being irked, the same as irritation.

clue.text: One line penned by tinker rather foolish

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so these letters sit inside the tinker's name

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single verse written by a travelling mender is rather daft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts IL inside SLY; Sly is a tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft or foolish behaviour is a mild synonym for stupidity.

clue.text: Incidence of carbon in soil is rising on island

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Incidence of carbon in soil is rising on island': the wordplay gives SIL(C)OS + IS, but 'Incidence of' cannot define SILICOSIS (a lung disease), so the definition looks misread and neither scan nor search gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Incidence of carbon in soil is rising on island

clue.text: Flanked by journalists, head of government moved cautiously

indicators.note: flanked by means having something on each side, so the letter sits between the two editors

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist; two of them give the letters twice

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word government

explanation.surface: With reporters on both sides, the prime minister crept forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flanked by' puts G between ED and ED; 'journalists' is plural so it gives two EDs.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch carefully sideways is to have edged along.

clue.text: Indulges in explanations

definitions.meaning: to excuse is to let off or forgive, so it indulges someone
reasons given to justify a failing are justifications

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is pardoning or letting off; the noun sense is justifications offered for a fault.

clue.text: Aliens sad about having a pronounced twang?

indicators.note: about means around and here signals the letters being moved around

explanation.surface: Unhappy extraterrestrials speak with a nasal drawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ALIENSSAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech produced through the nose has a twang, so 'pronounced' is the past participle meaning voiced.

clue.text: Consumers who'll be pleased to get a pound off?

definitions.text: Consumers who'll be pleased to get a pound off?

parts.words: Consumers who'll be pleased to get a pound off?
parts.note: a pound off sounds like a shop discount for shoppers, but here it is a pound of body weight lost by people eating less

explanation.walkthrough: 'a pound off' suggests money off a price; it is a pound of weight off people on a slimming regime.
explanation.definitionFit: People cutting calories to slim are pleased when their weight drops by a pound.

clue.text: Disaster in outskirts of Chatham -a river's found to contain chlorine

indicators.note: in places the middle portion within the town's first and last letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so take the first and last letters of Chatham
to contain means holding something inside, so the chlorine symbol goes into the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river, here with its possessive S
CL is the chemical symbol for chlorine

explanation.surface: A catastrophe on the edge of a Kent town: a river is found polluted with chlorine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts CL in TAYS, giving TACLYS; A and that go 'in' C...M. Chatham is a town in Kent; the Tay is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent upheaval or catastrophe is a great calamity.

clue.text: Film role came to nothing

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An actor's part in a movie ended up as nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief appearance by a famous actor is a small but notable part in a movie.

clue.text: Second fellow failing to finish coffee

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Another man couldn't finish his cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to finish' drops the last letter of CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate-flavoured espresso drink, or a fine Arabian bean, is a kind of coffee.

clue.text: Constabulary in turn have to identify crook

indicators.note: in turn means turned round, so the police abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the former Northern Ireland police force
've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: The police take turns trying to catch a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' turns RUC into CUR. The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a bend, as in the crook of an arm, so a bend or arc.

clue.text: Garment worn in many lengths and several styles

definitions.text: Garment worn in many lengths and several styles

parts.words: Garment worn in many lengths and several styles
parts.note: the lengths are laps of a pool and the styles are strokes such as crawl and breaststroke, not measurements and fashions of clothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'lengths' and 'styles' sound like dressmaking, but they are pool laps and swimming strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathing wear is the outfit worn to swim laps in a pool using various strokes.

clue.text: Continental ladies with minds ultimately blank

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word minds

parts.note: to blank someone is to ignore them

explanation.surface: European women whose thoughts eventually go empty.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNORE is the Italian plural of signora, a married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for married women, used as a courtesy title, so ladies on the Continent.

clue.text: Helps silly person one's found hanging around street

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: hanging around means surrounding, so these letters go round the street abbreviation

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals, with 's giving S

explanation.surface: A fool loiters on the street corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' puts ST inside I'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lends a hand, aids, supports: all mean helps.
